title: Deeper/broader cross-project conversion completeness and handle-identity failure chain
mode: primary-source web research and plan refinement
scope: Reconcile LibreDWG converter reports for partial output, invalid compound records, unsupported legacy records, and duplicate handles
Cross-check DXF handles, typed references, and INSERT/SEQEND semantics against Autodesk documentation
Refine existing fast writer-property and composed converter gates without adding external fixtures or routine peer runs

method.kind: Read-only review of public issue/documentation pages and local plan owners
method.limitations: LibreDWG issue bodies are reporter-provided observations for pinned 0.14.8556/e405fcff and named corpora; sample attachments were not downloaded or rerun. The ODA File Converter comparisons quoted in issue #1356 were not independently executed. Peer reports and mutable project documentation do not establish matching libdxfrw defects or normative pre-R13 semantics.

sources.revision: Public issue pages reviewed 2026-10-18; reports #1351/#1354/#1355/#1356 name LibreDWG 0.14.8556 at e405fcff, with #1355/#1356 arising from a reported 1,657-drawing sweep
sources.observed: The reports describe four distinct conversion failure classes: INSERT 66=1 without a complete ATTRIB/SEQEND sequence; pre-R13 REPEAT/ENDREP/LOAD records leaking into DXF and being ignored; a partial DXF without ENTITIES or terminal EOF despite exit status zero after structural root/table decode failures; and emitted zero/duplicate handles causing a layout's fixed BLOCK_RECORD reference to resolve to the wrong object class. The issue pages remain reports, not independently reproduced libdxfrw or general LibreDWG-current-master results. Earlier plan evidence records the exact #1351 reproducer later fixed on LibreDWG master, so its currently open issue status is not treated as proof that the reviewed master still fails.

sources.revision: Current public DXF documentation pages reviewed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: The INSERT reference says group 66=1 expects following ATTRIB entities terminated by SEQEND. The group-code table identifies code 5 as an entity handle and distinguishes typed handle/reference ranges. Persistent reference documentation describes how typed references are preserved and translated during object operations. These contracts support checking sequence grammar, identity, and target role as separate invariants.

sources.revision: Mutable master documentation/source reviewed 2026-10-18; issue #1356 reports ezdxf 1.4.4
sources.observed: The documented strict-read, recovery/audit, loaded-model statistics, and raw-structure browsing paths are distinct. Existing source review shows table audit can repair duplicate handles and notes that this may break references. A repaired/recovered file that opens is therefore a separate diagnostic result, not proof that the original output graph was valid.

sources.revision: Working tree at baseline commit de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
sources.observed: Existing owners already cover compound INSERT sequences, AC1.40 legacy fail-closed handling, output transactions, graph closure, and a bounded whole-output writer property under PAR-12/S13. This update adds the missing peer #1356 identity/root-class route to those owners and sharpens the composed success contract without opening a new finding or test target.

assessment.planImpact: Adds zero/duplicate source identity and role-correct root resolution to the existing PAR-12/S13 property; keeps INSERT sequence grammar, pre-R13 unsupported-record refusal, and strict-complete conversion as distinct assertions. Peer recovery/audit is labeled separately from strict parsing. Routine validation remains focused and fast.

implementationReadyChecks: For accepted generated ASCII and Binary DXF, verify complete pairs, balanced required sections, exactly one terminal group-0 EOF, unique emitted object handles, and role-correct resolution of required owner/root edges.

Exercise a zero/duplicate source-identity or structural-handle collision: either prove a complete deterministic remap of all captured references or refuse atomically; never publish ambiguous identities.
Keep INSERT group 66, emitted ATTRIB children, owning SEQEND, and following-sibling alignment as a compound-record assertion in the existing owner.
Keep PAR-123/7BS REPEAT/ENDREP/LOAD fail-closed until an authoritative semantic mapping is established; do not infer INSERT array conversion from shared group-code names.
At the composed strict-complete gate, bind each source record to one typed/retained/refused disposition, check roots/sections and output status, and preserve the destination on incomplete conversion.
If using ezdxf, hash and strictly read the untouched output before any audit/recovery; report repairs and identity changes separately.
Run only touched targets/selectors and the owning CTest per local slice; schedule independent readers, corpus sweeps, and native applications at existing composed checkpoints.
Do not download or commit peer/customer DWG/DXF files, add dependencies, register a new CTest, or promote support claims from this research.
